sections.h2: What makes a McKinney sale go quickly
sections.html:
Three things: clear title, a price buyers believe and a house someone can move into without a long repair list. Demand in McKinney is strong, but so is the supply of competing listings, and those three points tend to separate the fast sales from the slow ones.

The city had an estimated 236,001 residents on July 1, 2025, up 20.8 percent from 195,331 in 2020. About 26.2 percent are under 18, which keeps family-sized houses in demand.

  • An agent gets you the largest audience, in exchange for commission and weeks on the market.
  • Selling without one keeps the fee and makes you the negotiator.
  • A cash buyer works on a shorter calendar and takes the house as it is.

sections.h2: McKinney home values and housing costs
sections.html:
Values here run above most of Texas. For 2020-2024 the median owner-occupied home was worth $471,800, and median household income was $124,215.

Over a third of homes are rented, so there is a sizable landlord and investor segment. If you own a rental house and the buyer wants it empty, the lease end date will matter to them.

McKinney is the Collin County seat, and the town and county are both named for Collin McKinney. The railroad arrived in 1872. By the 1980s the town had become a commuter base for people working in Plano and Dallas.

Expect older homes around the historic center and large newer subdivisions farther out. Your buyers will compare your house with whichever of those two groups it resembles, so price against the right one.

sections.h2: Collin County offices for McKinney sellers
sections.html:
McKinney sits in Collin County. The Collin Central Appraisal District values the house, and the county clerk records the deed. The district's website has a property search, a map, homestead forms and a link to the appraisal review board that hears protests.

  • Pull your property account before listing and confirm which exemptions are on file.
  • A separate tax transparency site lists details for each taxing entity.
  • A buyer's agent will likely pull the same record, so fix errors in square footage or exemption status early. That prevents surprises during the option period.

Request the total owed from the county tax office. A balance from an earlier year stays attached to the house.

Every short-term rental inside McKinney city limits must register each year, and the program is free. The city defines one as a house, apartment, room or other dwelling rented through Airbnb, VRBO or similar platforms for thirty days or less. Long-term leases, apartment complexes renting standard units, hotels, motels and bed and breakfasts are outside the rule.

  • Each rental unit is registered separately, and every owner provides contact information.
  • A responsible person must be reachable 24 hours a day about concerns.
  • Registration does not override HOA or deed restrictions, and it does not ban short-term rentals.
  • All short-term rentals must pay Hotel Occupancy Tax.

Owners register through the city's Customer Self-Service portal or in person at Development Services on the second floor of City Hall. If the house you are selling has hosted guests, confirm the registration is current so the buyer gets a clean file.

sections.h2: Hotel occupancy tax on vacation rentals
sections.html:
McKinney charges a 7 percent city Hotel Occupancy Tax on lodging, vacation rentals included, on top of the 6 percent state rate that is remitted separately. Booking platforms that take payment for a short-term rental now collect and remit the city tax for the operator, a rule in place since September 2, 2025.

  • Reports and payments are due on the 20th of the month after each reporting month.
  • A report is required even in a month with no tax collected.
  • Late payment adds a 5 percent penalty at 1 to 30 days, 10 percent after 30 days, and 10 percent plus 10 percent annual interest at 60 days or more.

A seller who has run a rental should have these filings in order. A buyer or title company may ask whether any tax is unpaid.

Texas has no state property tax, so exemptions come off local bills. Any taxing unit may adopt an optional homestead exemption of up to 20 percent of appraised value with a $5,000 minimum, and the Collin appraisal district's taxing entity page shows which units offer one.

A veteran rated 100 percent disabled may qualify for a total homestead exemption under Section 11.131, and lesser ratings earn smaller exemptions listed in the Comptroller's table. If you are buying a disabled veteran's former home, ask the appraisal district what carries over.

sections.h2: What heirs of a McKinney house should do first
sections.html:
An heir has several routes, and the one you choose sets the schedule. Texas allows four years from the death to offer a will for probate.

  • Muniment of title, for an estate with no debts beyond real-estate liens.
  • Small estate affidavit, used when no will exists and assets come to $75,000 or less, homestead excluded.
  • Affidavit of heirship, which buyers need not accept.
  • Transfer on death deed, recorded during the owner's life.

Ask the Collin County clerk what is filed on the property and have a title company confirm it before you accept an offer.

Newcomers tend to be well paid, and per capita income is $55,643. About 85.5 percent of people lived in the same house a year earlier, so most owners stay put and listings come from a smaller pool than the population suggests.

Census counts went from 131,117 in 2010 to 195,308 in 2020, and land area grew from 62.21 to 66.96 square miles over that decade. That growth is why so many nearby listings are recent construction, which sets the bar for finishes on an older house.

sections.h2: Steps to sell and what to bring
sections.html:
Before any buyer sees the paperwork, collect the deed, the current tax statement and a payoff figure if a mortgage remains. Open your account on the appraisal district's property search to confirm the exemptions and square footage on record.

  1. Pick the route: agent, sale on your own or a cash buyer.
  2. Accept an offer and let a title company look for liens, unpaid taxes and probate gaps.
  3. Clear whatever turns up. A clean title closes sooner than one with liens or missing heirs.
  4. Sign the deed and have the county clerk record it.

A cash sale skips inspection repair requests and most showings, which can help when the house needs work or the calendar is tight.

faqs.q: Which county handles McKinney property records?
faqs.a: Collin County. McKinney is the county seat, about thirty-two miles north of Dallas, and the Collin Central Appraisal District and county clerk handle values and deeds.

faqs.q: What is a typical McKinney home worth?
faqs.a: The 2020-2024 median for owner-occupied homes is $471,800. Individual houses vary a great deal by age, size and neighborhood.

faqs.q: How quickly can a McKinney sale close?
faqs.a: It depends on the buyer and on title. A clean title closes sooner than one with liens, probate or missing heirs, so order a title search early.

faqs.q: Must a McKinney house go through probate before I sell it?
faqs.a: Usually some court or recorded step comes first. A transfer on death deed recorded before the death is the main exception, and a Texas attorney can say which route fits.

faqs.q: Does the Collin appraisal district publish homestead forms?
faqs.a: Yes. Its site lists residential homestead exemption information and forms. Call the district for the filing deadline that applies to you.
